sections.content:
The Agent Runtime is the controlled execution plane of AI-ConneX. It takes an approved, immutable Agent SPEC and turns it into observable runtime behavior: ingesting permitted observations, maintaining bounded state, invoking approved models and knowledge, planning within the SPEC, requesting approvals, calling only authorized tools, handling failures, escalating and recording an auditable execution trace.

The Runtime is deliberately NOT the Agent Builder and NOT the LLM. Builder creates the contract; the Runtime enforces it. The model may propose a next step, but the Runtime and Policy Engine decide whether that step is structurally permitted.

JANE  |  vAGENT BUILDER  |  vSIGNED AGENT SPEC  |  v+---------------------------+|       AGENT RUNTIME       ||                           || Trigger -> Observe ->     || Context -> Reason ->      || Validate -> Act -> Audit  |+-------------+-------------+              |       POLICY / APPROVAL              |        TOOL GATEWAY              |      INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS              |          VISUALIZER

sections.heading_text: 2. Why Runtime Is a Separate Stage
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-013 > 2. Why Runtime Is a Separate Stage
sections.content:
An LLM cannot safely be treated as an authorization layer.

Industrial actions need deterministic enforcement.

Runtime state, retries, timeouts and concurrency need infrastructure controls.

Tools require credentials, network isolation and parameter validation.

Human approvals must pause and resume execution reliably.

Every consequential operation needs provenance and auditability.

Runtime must survive model/tool failures without inventing behavior.

This separation is directly aligned with the security concern of excessive agency: OWASP describes excessive functionality, permissions and autonomy as root causes and recommends constraining agent capabilities rather than relying on model behavior alone. citeturn0search1turn0search16

Research question: how can AI-ConneX execute an industrial agent continuously and reliably while keeping autonomy bounded by an explicit Agent SPEC, current industrial context, policy, model contracts and human approvals?
tables:
| R&D risk | Runtime design response |
| --- | --- |
| Model output is probabilistic | Typed plan/action validation before side effects. |
| Context changes | Ground-State freshness checks. |
| Tools fail | Bounded retry, circuit breaker and escalation. |
| Agent loops | Iteration, time, tool-call and cost budgets. |
| Duplicate alerts/actions | Idempotency keys and deduplication. |
| Unauthorized action | Policy Engine + Tool Gateway deny-by-default. |
| Human unavailable | Approval timeout with safe stop/escalation. |
| Telemetry missing | Explicit uncertainty/stale-data state. |
| Runtime crashes | Durable workflow state and replay. |
| Version drift | Pin and verify SPEC/model/tool versions. |

CREATED  |VALIDATING  |READY  |RUNNING  |  | +--> WAITING_APPROVAL --> APPROVED --+  |                 |                    |  |                 +--> REJECTED -------+  |                                      |  +--> WAITING_DATA ---------------------+  |  +--> RETRYING  |  +--> ESCALATED  |  +--> FAILED  |  +--> COMPLETED  |  +--> TERMINATED

Only explicit state transitions are permitted. A state transition should carry an execution ID, SPEC version, reason and timestamp.

The LLM/model is a reasoning component, not the runtime authority. Its output must be converted into a typed internal representation before any tool call.

MODEL OUTPUT    |    vJSON / typed action plan    |    +--> schema validation    +--> scope validation    +--> policy validation    +--> parameter validation    +--> safety constraints    +--> approval check    |    vTOOL GATEWAY

All side-effecting operations should pass through a Tool Gateway. Credentials should remain outside prompts and outside the Agent SPEC wherever possible; the gateway maps a permitted capability to an appropriate service identity.

Agent Runtime     |     | typed ToolCall     vTool Gateway     |     +--> authenticate     +--> authorize     +--> validate schema     +--> validate asset scope     +--> idempotency     +--> rate limit     +--> execute     +--> capture result     |     vIndustrial API / Service

{  "tool_uid": "create_maintenance_alert",  "version": "1.3",  "capability": "inform",  "input_schema": "ALERT-V4",  "output_schema": "ALERT-RESULT-V2",  "side_effect": true,  "idempotency": "required",  "timeout_seconds": 20,  "allowed_autonomy": ["INFORM","RECOMMEND"]}

The Runtime needs an authoritative industrial context because an agent cannot safely reason about an asset from names alone. ISO 23247-2:2021 provides a manufacturing digital-twin reference architecture with domain/entity and functional views; AI-ConneX uses a similar separation by resolving agent execution against a versioned Ground-State. citeturn0search0

ISO 23247-4:2021 addresses information exchange between entities in the manufacturing digital-twin architecture, which supports the architectural decision to treat Runtime integrations as explicit information-exchange contracts. citeturn0search5

Ground-State check:asset exists?asset belongs to tenant/site?telemetry fresh?topology version compatible?operating mode compatible?required sensor available?maintenance lock active?policy current?

The Runtime does not redo compilation. It consumes the lineage references produced earlier and uses them to understand which dataset, profile, DAG and family the agent is operating against.

runtime_context.data:  manifest_uid: MANIFEST-001  profile_uid: PROFILE-001  dag_ids: [DAG-01]  family_ids: [FAM-01]  feature_contract: FE-07  preparation_version: PREP-12

This makes the agent's observation and model inputs traceable back to Data Studio.

runtime_context.model:  model_uid: MODEL-COMP-HEALTH  version: 2.1.0  input_schema: SCHEMA-17  output_schema: SCHEMA-19  deployment: production  limitations:    - asset_family: compressor-A

The Runtime verifies that the actual input schema and asset context match the model contract before inference.

Retrieve only from collections referenced by the SPEC.

Apply tenant/site/asset access controls before retrieval.

Treat retrieved content as evidence, not authority.

Attach document/version IDs to the execution trace.

Do not allow retrieved instructions to modify permissions.

Require freshness policy for safety-critical procedures.

OWASP's 2025 guidance identifies prompt injection and vector/embedding weaknesses as significant risks; therefore RAG must remain subordinate to the SPEC and policy rather than becoming an implicit command channel. citeturn0search14

ACTION PROPOSED      |      vCONSEQUENCE CLASS      | +----+---------+-----------+ |              |           |LOW           MEDIUM       HIGH |              |           |AUTO          APPROVAL    EXPLICITINFORM        REQUEST     APPROVAL |              |           | +--------------+-----------+                |             EXECUTE

Approvals must be durable: if the Runtime restarts while waiting, it should resume from the approval state rather than executing again.
The Runtime must reject an action that exceeds the SPEC's declared autonomy even if the model proposes it.
tables:
| Autonomy | Runtime behavior |
| --- | --- |
| OBSERVE | Read and summarize only. |
| INFORM | Create approved notifications/alerts. |
| RECOMMEND | Produce recommendation; no side effect unless separately authorized. |
| REQUEST_APPROVAL | Prepare action and pause. |
| EXECUTE | Execute only the explicitly permitted action and conditions. |

| Failure | Impact | Runtime mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid SPEC | Unsafe/undefined behavior | Reject before execution |
| Signature failure | Tampered behavior | Fail closed |
| Stale Ground-State | Wrong asset decision | Pause/escalate |
| Model unavailable | No prediction | Declared fallback or escalate |
| Model timeout | Latency/queue buildup | Bounded timeout + circuit breaker |
| Tool timeout | Partial operation | Idempotent retry + reconciliation |
| Duplicate event | Alert/action storm | Deduplication + idempotency |
| LLM loop | Cost/latency explosion | Max iterations/time/tool budget |
| Prompt injection | Policy bypass | Authority separation + validation |
| Excessive agency | Unauthorized side effects | Deny-by-default gateway |
| Conflicting telemetry | Bad decision | Conflict state + uncertainty |
| Approval unavailable | Unsafe continuation | Pause; never auto-approve |
| Cross-tenant request | Data leakage | Tenant-bound authorization |
| Runtime crash | Lost execution state | Durable workflow state |
| Network partition | Unknown side-effect status | Reconciliation/idempotency |
| Tool contract drift | Wrong parameters | Versioned schemas |
| Alert fatigue | Operator ignores alarms | Deduplication, severity and cooldown |

sections.content:
Fail closed for safety-critical and consequential actions.

Fail gracefully for informational functions.

Never assume a side effect failed merely because the response was lost; reconcile when possible.

Never retry a non-idempotent action without an idempotency/reconciliation strategy.

Use exponential backoff with bounded maximum attempts.

Escalate when uncertainty crosses the SPEC threshold.

Record the reason for every retry, denial, escalation and termination.

IDENTITY                       |                       v                 POLICY ENGINE                       |                       vAGENT SPEC --> RUNTIME --> ACTION VALIDATOR                  |              |                  |              v                  |         TOOL GATEWAY                  |              |                  v              v             AUDIT / TRACE --> INDUSTRIAL APILLM ----> proposes ----> NEVER directly authorizes

OWASP's current agentic security guidance emphasizes that agent systems can plan, act and coordinate across workflows and therefore need controls beyond ordinary chatbot security. citeturn0search16turn0search17

OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral instrumentation and collection for traces, metrics and logs, making it an appropriate baseline for the Runtime's execution telemetry. citeturn0search8turn0search18

For OT/industrial environments, network segmentation should separate enterprise IT, AI services and control networks. The Runtime should not obtain unrestricted network reachability to PLCs or safety systems.

AI-ConneX should treat direct machine-control operations as a distinct risk tier. A monitoring or recommendation agent can operate with read/inform/recommend permissions without receiving write access to control systems. If future versions support control actions, those actions should be mediated by dedicated safety-approved interfaces, explicit approvals and independent interlocks.

The Runtime must never equate an ML prediction with a safety authorization.

sections.heading_text: 34. Proof of Concept — Compressor Health Agent
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-013 > 34. Proof of Concept — Compressor Health Agent
sections.content:
Create Plant-01 Ground-State with three compressors and telemetry.

Register Agent SPEC AGT-COMP-001:v1.0.0.

Verify signature and referenced model/tool versions.

Generate normal telemetry events.

Trigger an abnormal vibration event.

Resolve asset COMP-02 and retrieve current telemetry.

Invoke the evaluated compressor-health model.

Validate prediction against the model output schema.

Generate a maintenance recommendation.

Invoke create_maintenance_alert through Tool Gateway.

Replay the same event to verify idempotency/cooldown.

Inject stale telemetry and verify execution pauses/escalates.

Simulate model outage and verify declared fallback.

Simulate tool outage and verify bounded retry.

Attempt PLC-write action and verify policy denial.

Restart Runtime while waiting for approval and verify durable resume.

Inspect trace and audit records.

Modify SPEC and verify signature rejection.

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-013 > 37. Prompt Injection Defense at Runtime
sections.content:
Never concatenate retrieved instructions into an authorization context.

Keep system/SPEC/policy authority separate from untrusted content.

Treat model output as untrusted until validated.

Validate all tool arguments against typed schemas.

Apply policy after model planning and before side effects.

Limit tool capabilities to the SPEC.

Log injection detections and denied actions.

Use red-team regression scenarios.

OWASP's 2025 Top 10 explicitly identifies prompt injection and explains that RAG/fine-tuning do not fully eliminate the risk. citeturn0search14turn0search49

OWASP's 2025 guidance identifies excessive agency as a risk caused by excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy. AI-ConneX counters all three at the Runtime boundary: only required tools are bound, permissions are explicit, and autonomy is encoded in the SPEC and enforced before side effects. citeturn0search1

NOT:LLM -> arbitrary APIYES:LLM -> typed proposal    -> SPEC check    -> policy check    -> approval check    -> Tool Gateway    -> side effect

Maximum iterations.

Maximum tool calls.

Execution deadline.

Model token/cost budget.

Per-agent rate limits.

Per-tenant quotas.

Circuit breakers.

Event deduplication.

Concurrency limits.

OWASP's current list includes unbounded consumption among the major GenAI risks, reinforcing the need for runtime budgets rather than assuming model calls will naturally terminate. citeturn0search14

This is an engineering compliance/readiness report, not a legal certification.

NIST AI RMF is intended to help organizations manage AI risks throughout design, development, deployment and use; AI-ConneX maps that lifecycle orientation into concrete Runtime controls. NIST also released a 2026 concept note for a Critical Infrastructure Profile, making this especially relevant to industrial deployment planning. citeturn0search7turn0search10

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-013 > 46. Agent Runtime and Industrialist Experience
sections.content:
Industrialists do not need to understand prompts or agent loops.

They see the asset, condition, evidence, recommendation, action and reason.

They can approve, reject, pause or escalate according to the SPEC.

Operations teams can inspect why an action was denied.

IT teams can inspect identity and audit trails.

Data teams can trace results back to Manifest/DAG/Family lineage.

ML teams can trace decisions to exact evaluated model versions.

The architectural boundary is deliberate: the Runtime is where the AI-ConneX agent becomes operational, but it never becomes unconstrained. The Agent SPEC defines the contract; policy and gateway enforce authority; the Runtime supplies durable execution, recovery and observability.

Agent Runtime is the execution heart of Agentic Studio. It converts the Agent SPEC from a static blueprint into a controlled, observable and recoverable industrial process. Its most important property is not autonomy; it is bounded autonomy.

For AI-ConneX, the complete chain is: Jane captures intent → Agent Builder compiles intent and industrial context → Agent SPEC defines the contract → Agent Runtime executes that contract → Policy/Approval controls authority → Tool Gateway controls side effects → Visualizer exposes the state → Audit preserves accountability.

That separation makes the architecture suitable for industrial environments where data quality, operational continuity, human accountability, security and traceability matter as much as model intelligence.
